Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates increased soft-tissue density in the retrotracheal space, which is a classic radiographic sign of a posterior mediastinal mass such as a neurofibroma. This finding, combined with the right-sided paratracheal fullness seen on the frontal view (Figure 1), best fits the description of a neurofibroma among the provided choices, whereas lipomas would appear radiolucent and duplication cysts typically present as smooth, round masses without this specific retrotracheal infiltration pattern.
